row.Finding description: In three repeated human-fibroblast competition experiments with four wells per condition, APOE4-mouse VLDL competed more strongly than APOE3-mouse VLDL for human LDL receptor binding and internalization, with Ki values of 3.6 ± 0.6 mg versus 5.7 ± 1.12 mg.
row.Finding quote: K i determined from 3 repeated experiments, each consisting of quadruple measurements, were 3.6 ± 0.6 mg for 4/4 VLDL and 5.7 ± 1.12 mg for 3/3 VLDL (P = 0.05 by one-way ANOVA). Therefore, the 4/4 VLDL has the ability to compete with human LDL for binding to the human LDL receptor better than the 3/3 VLDL.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4 in donor mice) -> (lower VLDL competition Ki for human LDL receptor binding and internalization)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized human fibroblasts supplied by J. Herz, exposed at 37°C to fluorescently labeled human LDL (50 μg/mL) and competing VLDL (0.5–100 μg/mL total protein). VLDL was isolated from plasma pooled from at least six female mice per genotype: human APOE3- or APOE4-targeted-replacement F2 129 × C57BL/6 hybrids, generally 8–20 weeks old, maintained on an HFC diet containing 15.8% fat, 1.25% cholesterol, and 0.5% sodium cholate. Cells received DMEM with 0.5% BSA for 24 hours before the assay. Cellular fluorescence measured LDL association and internalization. Brain cells and receptor recycling were not examined.

row.Finding quote: These differences among apoE isoforms were also observed under a ﬂuorescence microscope (Fig. 3B).
row.Experimental system: Human Coriell GM00701 fibroblasts incubated with recombinant human apoE-containing synthetic fluorescent emulsion particles at 2.0 mg/dL apoE for 3 h at 4 °C; fluorescence microscopy at 100× magnification and ImageJ quantification. The legend describes representative images from three independent experiments and relative fluorescence calculated from 30 cells; receptor recycling was not measured.

set.Finding description: Fluorescence microscopy of the same binding assay reproduced the isoform pattern, with relative fluorescence printed under the panels as 15.094 +/- 1.787 for apoE3 versus 9.880 +/- 1.090 for apoE4 (1.5-fold lower with apoE4, from 30 cells by ImageJ); the asterisks in the panel mark each apoE condition against control cells, and no apoE4-versus-apoE3 significance is given.

proposal.reason: Fig. 3B prints the relative fluorescence for each isoform, so the row should not stay qualitative: apoE3 15.094 and apoE4 9.880 give a 1.5x ratio. The *** key applies to the comparison with control cells, so the P value stays N/A for apoE3 versus apoE4.
proposal.evidence: Fig. 3B of the PDF page image: numbers under the four micrographs read '1.000 +/- 0.983' (without apoE), '4.438 +/- 0.438***' (apoE2), '15.094 +/- 1.787***' (apoE3), '9.880 +/- 1.090***' (apoE4); legend: 'The number below the images represents the relative fluorescence intensity compared with that in control cells, which was calculated from the results obtained for 30 cells by the IMAGE J analysis. ***, P < 0.001.'

paper.hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

row.Finding description: Image analysis of electron micrographs found a larger mean-complex-area distribution for LPS-treated APOE4 than APOE3.
row.Finding quote: This difference in aggregate size was confirmed by image analysis, revealing a larger distribution of the mean complex area in samples containing rAPOE4 compared with rAPOE3 (Fig. 6B).
row.Experimental system: ImageJ analysis of negative-stain TEM images of purified recombinant human APOE3 and APOE4 with E. coli LPS; three independently prepared samples, ten fields examined per preparation; 30-minute incubation at 37 °C; reported size metric differs between Results and methods.

row.Finding description: Mouse macrophages took up significantly more Amytracker-stained LPS-treated APOE4 aggregates than APOE3 aggregates in four independent experiments.
row.Finding quote: Furthermore, the data indicate that uptake by the cells was significantly more pronounced for the LPS-treated E4 isoform when compared with the LPS-treated E3 isoform (Fig. 8A).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater macrophage-associated uptake of APOE aggregates)
row.Experimental system: Murine RAW 264.7 macrophage cell line, passages 4–7; recombinant human APOE3 or APOE4, 100 nM, with E. coli LPS, 100 nM, and Amytracker 680; mixtures incubated 30 minutes at room temperature before 1-hour cell exposure at 37 °C; fluorescence after washing; no endosomal or lysosomal marker.
